["mcq","seminoma: • this is the commonest malignant tumour of the testis constituting 50% of all testicular germ cell tumours. • it almost never develops before puberty and has a peak incidence in the forties. gross:a well circumscribed soft spherical mass, replacing all or part of the testis. the cut surface is solid, greyish white and homogeneous (fig.8.4a). microscopic",["classical seminoma: - the tumour is made up of masses of large cells with abundant, pale or clear cytoplasm and large central nuclei, separated by a thin stroma which is usually infiltrated by lymphocytesand often contains epithelioid granulomas resembling those of sarcoidosis. - the lymphocytic infiltrate and the granulomas are favourable prognostic features and may represent a defensive immune reaction to the tumour","spermatocytic seminoma: - the neoplastic cells resemble secondary spermatocytes. it lacks the lymphocytic infiltrate and granulomas - it never sends metastases and does not occur in combination with other germ cell tumours. hence, it has better prognosis. - it occurs at an older age than the classical seminoma. prognosis of seminoma:  seminomas are remarkably radiosensitive.  about 95% of patients with spread limited to the para-aortic lymph nodes.  it remains localized for a long time and even those cases with lung metastases have a relatively good prognosis after radiotherapy"],"classical seminoma: - the tumour is made up of masses of large cells with abundant, pale or clear cytoplasm and large central nuclei, separated by a thin stroma which is usually infiltrated by lymphocytesand often contains epithelioid granulomas resembling those of sarcoidosis. - the lymphocytic infiltrate and the granulomas are favourable prognostic features and may represent a defensive immune reaction to the tumour"]

["essay","difference between classic and spermatocytic","a- classical seminoma: - the tumour is made up of masses of large cells with abundant, pale or clear cytoplasm and large central nuclei, separated by a thin stroma which is usually infiltrated by lymphocytesand often contains epithelioid granulomas resembling those of sarcoidosis. - the lymphocytic infiltrate and the granulomas are favourable prognostic features and may represent a defensive immune reaction to the tumour. b- spermatocytic seminoma: - the neoplastic cells resemble secondary spermatocytes. it lacks the lymphocytic infiltrate and granulomas - it never sends metastases and does not occur in combination with other germ cell tumours. hence, it has better prognosis. - it occurs at an older age than the classical seminoma"]

["essay","a 42-year-old woman who has had proteinuria for about 5 years develops renal failure. she","also has developed hypertension and always complaining of repeated vaginal fungus infections over the last 10 years. she told her doctor that her last pregnancy ends by c.s. for large size baby over 5 kg. renal biopsy was done and reveals diffuse increase of mesangial matrix and thickening of glomerular basement membrane. a. what is the most likely diagnosis? b. what are other renal diseases that may occur in this patient? c. what are the other forms of glomerular disease that may occur in this disease? answer: a- nephrotic syndrome resulting from diabetic glomerulosclerosis, b- * renal arteriolar sclerosis * pyelonephritis * papillary necrosis c- nodular glomerulosclerosis"]

["essay","a 30-year-old female patient presents with new onset of generalized oedema. physical","examination reveals hypertension. urine analysis reveals massive proteinuria and elevated serum cholesterol. electron microscopy of renal biopsy specimen reveals subepithelial electron dense deposits separated by spikes. a. what is the most likely diagnosis? b. what are the light microscopic findings in her renal biopsy? c. describe the results of immunofluorescence testing. d. what do you think about electron microscopic findings in advanced stages of the disease? answers a- membranous glomerulonephritis"]

["essay","a 21-year-old male presents with haemoptysis. a few days later, he experiences sudden onset","of acute renal failure. urine analysis reveals mild proteinuria, hematuria and rbcs casts. renal biopsy reveals prominent proliferation of the capsular epithelium. a- which of the following is involved in the pathogenesis of glomeruler disease? i. anti-basement membrane antibodies ii. loss of negative charge in the g.b.m. iii. epithelial cell injury iv. immune complexes b- what is the name of this disease involving both lungs and kidney? c- what is the pathogenesis? d- what is the immunofluorescence findings? e- what is the clinical course of the disease? answers a- i b- good pasture's syndrome"]

["essay","a 52-year-old woman has a 15-year- history of rheumatoid arthritis. she complains of swelling","of her feet. physical examination reveals hepatosplenomegaly. urine analysis shows fatty casts and 5gm protein/24hours. her blood level of albumin is reduced, while her serum cholesterol level is increased. a. what is the most likely diagnosis? b. what is the light microscopic picture of her renal biopsy? c. which of the following serum protein is mostly likely increased in this patient? i. amyloid precursor protein ii. calcitonin iii. transthyretin iv. serum associated amyloid protein(aa) answers a- nephrotic syndrome due to renal amyloidosis b- thickening of capillary wall by amyloid depositions (congo red stain) c- iv"]

["essay","an 8- year-old boy has a 2-day- history of malaise, fever and loin pain. his mother noticed","that he had decreased urine output and that this urine is dark and has smoky color. on examination, his blood pressure is slightly elevated, with oedema of the face and puffiness of eye lids. he has been in good health except for a sore throat a week ago. a. what is the most likely diagnosis? b. what mechanism is involved (pathogenesis)? c. describe the microscopic changes in the kidney? d. what are the laboratory findings in this case? e. what is the usual clinical course? answers a- acute diffuse proliferative (post streptococcal) glomerulonephritis"]

["essay","a 56-year-old man has had back pain. he passed dark colored urine for the past month. on","physical examination, there is right costo-vertebral angle fullness and tenderness. urine analysis shows ph 6, 2+ haematuria, no protein, no wbcs, no casts and no crystals. ct. scan revealed a solid mass in the upper pole of right kidney. a- what is the possible diagnosis? b- what are the microscopic findings? c- which of the following laboratory findings is mostly to be found in this patient? i. elevated serum cholesterol ii. elevated serum glucose iii. elevated rbcs count iv. elevated wbcs count answers a- renal cell carcinoma c- iii due to secretion of erythropoietin (paraneoplastic syndrome) hormone by the tumor causing polycythaemia"]
